the influence of carbon monoxide (Co), a gas which is produced endogenously in the body, and its interaction with nitric oxide, on the adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), response to a mild inescapible stress.
the influence of carbon monoxide (C O) and nitric oxide (N O) on the hypothalamic‐pituitary‐adrenal (HPA) axis response to mild ines‐capable electrofootshock.
the study of the influence of carbon monoxide, and its interactions with nitric oxide, on the neuroendocrine response of the normal rat to a physico‐emotional stress.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NO and CO are both involved in the HPA response to mild insecapable shocks, and that the NO‐dependent influence of CO on the HPA response is exerted in part on hypothalamic PVN neurons.
CO, in the presence of NO, exerts a stimulatory effect at the hypothalamic level on the HPA response to a physico‐emotional stress.
the influence of NO and CO on the HPA stress response to mild electroshock is exerted on hypothalamus neurons and/or their efferent projections.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CO and NO are two important mediators of the HPA response to stress.
NO and CO are both necessary for the full expression of the HPA axis to stress, and that they exert their influence by modulating hypothalamic neuronal function.
NO and CO, both by‐products of heme metabolism, are necessary for the normal expression of the HPA axis in response to a mild stress.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CO, like NO, plays a role in the modulation of the HPA axis, and that it does so by influencing hypothalamic neuronal function.
CO and NO, which are both produced by the same enzyme (NOS) in response to mild stressors, act in concert to modulate HPA activity.
the CO‐NO system is an important modulator of the HPA axis.
